CITY OF INGLEWOOD
  ECONOMIC AND COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT DEPARTMENT
  PLANNING COMMISSION
  MEETING AGENDA
September 2, 2020 7:00 P.M.
City Council Chambers – Ninth Floor (Planning Commission & Staff)
1 West Manchester Boulevard

  COVID-19 PUBLIC PARTICIPATION OPTIONS

Due to the existing COVID-19 health emergency and the social
distancing measures currently in effect, and pursuant to the
Governor’s Executive Order N-29-20 ((https://www.gov.ca.gov/wp-
content/uploads/2020/03/3.17.20-N-29-20-EO.pdf)),  please  note
that members of the public will only be allowed to observe and
address the Planning Commission Meeting of September 2, 2020 at
7:00 P.M. by telephone, video and other electronic means, as
follows:

Viewing and Listening to the Meeting without Making Public
Comments:
   On Spectrum Cable Local Channel 35 with audio and limited
  video. Please check with your cable provider for details.
   Live on-line through Facebook Live, with audio and limited
  video, at https://www.facebook.com/cityofinglewood/
   The above access options provide the public with the
  opportunity to both observe and listen to the meeting.
   However, members of the public who wish to orally address the
  Planning Commission must use the public access options noted
  below:

Listening to the Meeting and Making Oral Public Comments:
Members of the public may listen and make oral public comments
telephonically by dialing:

  Dial-in: 1-888-251-2949 or 215-861-0694
  Access Code: 5048331##

Please observe the following tips when phoning in:

    When you call-in, the operator will provide further
  instructions on how you can make public comments via phone.
    If you are calling from a cell phone, please call from an
  area with good reception.
    If you are watching the meeting on Facebook or Channel 35
  while also accessing the phone line, it is requested that you
  mute the sound of your video feed as it is offset by 3 seconds
  from the phone transmission. Additionally, when you are
  making public comments on the phone line you will be inaudible
  due to feedback.

Written Public Comments: Members of the public can submit comments
for consideration by the Planning Commission by sending them to
Mindy  Wilcox,  AICP,  Planning  Manager  at
mwilcox@cityofinglewood.org. To ensure distribution to the members
of the Planning Commission prior to consideration of the agenda,
comments must be received prior to 12:00 P.M. on September 2, 2020,
the day of the meeting. Correspondence should indicate the meeting
date and agenda item. Comments received after 12:00 P.M. and prior
to close of the public hearing will be made part of the official
public record of the meeting.
[Agenda Items and Additional Public Access Options Listed on
Following Pages]
 1.  Pledge of Allegiance.

2.  Roll Call.

3.  Communications from staff.

4.  Public Comments Regarding Agenda Items. Persons wishing to
  address the Planning Commission on any item on the agenda
  other than a public hearing may do so at this time.

5.  PUBLIC HEARINGS
  a. A public hearing to consider an application by Nagy
  Bakhoum, representing B & H Tow, for Special Use Permit
  No. 2020-008 (SP-2020-008) to allow towing service on an
  approximately 34,353 square-foot, C-S (Commercial Service)
  zoned property at 10201 Hawthorne Boulevard.
  Preliminary Recommendations:
  1. Affirm Notice of Exemption EA-CE-2019-091;
  2. Adopt the attached resolution approving SP-2020-008
  subject to conditions.

  b. A public hearing to consider an application by Kevin Brown
  for Special Use Permit No. 2020-009 (SP-2020-009) to allow
  exterior alterations to an existing nonresidential
  structure in the Medical Enterprise Overlay Zone that
  exceeds a valuation of twenty thousand dollars ($20,000.00)
  on an approximately 1.27 acre, C-2 (General Commercial)
  zoned property at 401 South Prairie Avenue.
  Preliminary Recommendations:
  1. Affirm Notice of Exemption EA-CE-2020-047; and
  2. Adopt the attached resolution approving SP-2020-009
  subject to conditions.

  c. A public hearing to consider an application by Johnathan
  DeVeaux, Owner, for Special Use Permit No. 2020-011 (SP-
  2020-011) to allow the sale of distilled spirits within an
  existing restaurant on a 3,742 square-foot H-C (Historic
  Core) zoned property at 129 North Market Street.
  Preliminary Recommendations:
  1. Affirm Notice of Exemption EA-CE-2020-070; and
  2. Adopt the attached resolution approving SP-2020-011
  subject to conditions.

6.  NON - PUBLIC HEARINGS
  a. A non-public hearing to consider an application by Joe
  Gambill, representing Wood Partners, for Design Review No.
  2020-004 (DR-2020-004) to approve the design proposal for
  a new 6-story, 144-unit residential building on an
  approximately 38,750 square foot lot, H-C (Historic Core)
  zoned property at 201 North La Brea Avenue.
  Preliminary Recommendations:
  1. Preliminary CEQA Recommendation:
  a. Affirm Categorical Exemption EA-CE-2020-065;
  and
  b. Adopt findings and the attached resolution
  approving DR-2020-004 subject to conditions.

7.  Commission Initiatives.

8.  Public Comments. Anyone wishing to address the Planning
  Commission on any matter within their jurisdiction and not
  elsewhere considered on the agenda may do so at this time.

please contact the Planning Division at (310) 412-5230, One
Manchester Boulevard, Fourth Floor,  Inglewood City Hall,

be received 48 hours prior to the day of the hearing(s). "Si no
entiende esta noticia o si necesita más información, favor de

next regular Planning Commission meeting.

REQUEST
The applicant is requesting approval of a Special Use Permit (SUP) to allow on-site
consumption of distilled spirits within an existing restaurant (Type 47), on an approximately
3,742 square-foot, H-C (Historic Core) zoned property.

Background
The Inglewood Municipal Code (IMC), Chapter 12, Articles 10.7 and 25, requires approval
of a Special Use Permit (SUP) to allow the on-site consumption of distilled spirits within a
restaurant. The subject 1,660 square foot building was constructed in 1927 and City
records indicate that multiple restaurants have operated at the location since 2008, with
the applicant occupying the space since 2019.

On August 2, 2017 the Planning Commission approved Special Use Permit No. 2017-008
to allow an event center with live entertainment and the sale of beer and wine for on-site
consumption within a café.

Site Characteristics and Existing Use
The subject site is located on the west side of Market Street and is zoned H-C (Historic
Core). The properties to the north, south, and east of the subject site are zoned H-C and
are developed with commercial uses. The property to the west, across the alley, is also
zoned H-C and is currently developed with a parking structure.

The 3,742 square-foot lot is developed with an existing 1,660 square-foot building and is
licensed to be used as a restaurant.

Project Description
The applicant has established a restaurant and is requesting permission from the Planning
Commission to allow the sale of distilled spirits in conjunction with the existing restaurant.

Discussion
The restaurant is comprised of an approximately 215 square-foot non-fixed seating dining
area including a 30 square-foot stage, a 728 square-foot fixed seating dining area, two (2)
restrooms, a 616 square-foot kitchen, a wait station and storage/food prep area, and a 66
square-foot office. The applicant will apply for a license for the on-site sale of distilled
spirits with the California Department of Alcoholic Beverage Control if this SUP is granted.
The applicant has indicated that the alcohol will be served during the business hours of
operation. The regular hours of operation for the restaurant are proposed to be Monday
thru Sunday 8:00 a.m. to 2:00 a.m. and will provide a full menu including breakfast, lunch
and dinner service throughout their hours of operation. The applicant proposes to provide
brunch service on Sunday from 11 a.m. to 2 p.m.
 Special Use Permit No. 2020-011 (SP-2020-011)  September 2, 2020
129 N. Market Street

Site Design
The subject site is 3,742 square feet and is developed with a 1,660 square-foot one story
building. The primary entrance to the building is on Market Street, and there is also a back
exit leading to the parking area and alley in the rear. Customers will enter from the main
entry off of Market Street.

Parking and Circulation
Parking for the property is located in the rear of the building with two off-street parking
spaces available. The restaurant with onsite alcohol sales does not require any additional
on-site parking and meets the IMC requirements. No change to the existing traffic level of
service is anticipated.

Security
Currently, the building has four (4) surveillance cameras on the interior and exterior of the
building. Two cameras are located in the main entertainment/dining area, with one of those
cameras monitoring the main entrance. An additional camera is located in the kitchen area,
and an exterior camera is located in the rear of the building by the exit to the parking area
and alley. The cameras are monitored in real time by a security company. The applicant
also proposes to have one security guard on-site during evening hours of 5:00 p.m. to 3:00
a.m.

Area Compatibility & Crime
The site is developed in accordance with existing zoning and development standards for
building height and setbacks for commercially-zoned properties. Land uses along Market
Street are developed primarily with commercial uses.

According to the Inglewood Police Department (IPD) records from 2017 to 2019, the City-
wide crime rate decreased by approximately six percent (from 3,451 incidents in 2014 to
3,239 incidents in 2016). In the subject Crime Reporting District (CRD), No. I-10, the crime
rate increased from 63 incidents in 2017 to 152 incidents in 2018. However, there was a
significant drop in crime from 152 incidents in 2018 to 116 in 2019. Table 1 shows the
crime statistics for individual crime types in the proposed subject location CRD for the last
three years. The IPD has not indicated that they are opposed to the proposed use for this
location.

MINUTES
  INGLEWOOD PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  WEDNESDAY, SEPTEMBER 2, 2020

(1) PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE:

The City of Inglewood Planning Commission held its Planning
Commission meeting on Wednesday, September 2, 2020 in the Council
Chambers on the ninth floor, in City Hall. Following the Pledge of
Allegiance by Commissioner Shaw-Williams, the meeting was called to
order at 7:00 p.m.

(2) ROLL CALL:

Present:  Commissioner Patricia Patrick
  Commissioner David Rice
  Commissioner Aide’ Trejo
  Commissioner Cheryl Shaw-Williams
  Chairman Larry Springs

Staff:  Mindy Wilcox, AICP, Planning Manager
  Jeff Lewis, Assistant City Attorney's Office
  Eddy Ikemefuna, Senior Planner
  Fred Jackson, Senior Planner
  Taylor Kay, Assistant Planner
  Arturo Salazar, Planner
  Bernard McCrumby, Planner
  Marissa Fewell, Planner
  Christopher E. Jackson, Sr., Director of E.C.D.
  Evangeline Lane, Secretary

(3) STAFF COMMUNICATIONS:

Ms. Wilcox stated we have received 3 items of communication regarding
Item 5C. SP-2020-011. They are 3 letters of support from Inglewood
Today, Dominique Antonini and Yvonne Morris.

(4) PUBLIC COMMENTS:

The AT&T Operator opened the lines of communication to the public
in order for anyone on the line to speak and give public comments
at this time. There were No Callers on the line.

(5) PUBLIC HEARING:

5A. SPECIAL USE PERMIT NO. 2020-008 (SP-2020-008) 10201 HAWTHORNE
BOULEVARD: A public hearing to consider an application by Nagy
Bakhoum, representing B & H Tow, for Special Use Permit No. 2020-008
(SP-2020-008) to allow a towing service on an approximately 34,353
square-foot, C-S (Commercial Service) zoned property at 10201
Hawthorne Boulevard.

Ms. Marissa Fewell, Assistant Planner made the staff presentation.

Chairman Springs asked the Planning Commission if there were any
questions for staff.

Commissioner Patrick asked staff if this is the same B & H Tow that
was at one point on the Northwest corner of Florence and La Brea but
has since moved?
   Ms. Fewell stated, yes.

  1
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
September 2, 2020

Commissioner Rice asked Ms. Fewell if she used a map or physically
went to the site to verify the lot size and the distance between tow
companies.
   Ms. Fewell stated that she used a map.

Commissioner Rice stated the maps can sometimes be off.

Chairman Springs asked the applicant who was on the AT&T phone line
and in attendance via teleconferencing to speak.

Nagy Bakhoum, representative for B & H Tow, was on the AT&T call line
via telephone and addressed the Planning Commission.

Commissioner Patrick asked the applicant why did B & H Towing move
from Florence and La Brea?
   Mr. Bakhoum stated that this property came up as an opportunity
  to be a permanent location instead of a temporary site as the
  previous location was.

Commissioner Patrick asked if the new site seems to be much smaller
than the previous location.
   Mr. Bakhoum stated that the new site is about three quarters
  of an acre. He stated that he believes the site will be ample
  for business.

Commissioner Trejo asked how many cars can fit at the location.
   Mr. Bakhoum stated that he didn’t know if there was an actual
  count but more than fifty cars could be placed on the lot.

Commissioner Trejo asked about the other towing service/license
   Mr. Bakhoum stated that the company has a tow truck license but
  not a tow yard license.

Commissioner Shaw-Williams asked if auto repair will be done at this
location.
   Mr. Bakhoum stated that his understanding is that this location
  is just for towing.

Chairman Springs asked if the location on La Brea and Florence is
owned or leased.
   Mr. Bakhoum stated that the owner could respond to that.
   Rob, the owner stated that they do not own the property on
  Florence but they do own the property on Hawthorne.

Chairman asked if the property next to the Hawthorne property was
a tow yard.
   Rob stated that the property listed on the staff report is a
  used car lot and they may own a tow truck to bring cars on to
  the facility.

Chairman asked Staff what is the service next to the Hawthorne site.
   Ms. Wilcox said that the site does have a towing license, however
  it is outside of the distance requirement.

Commissioner Patrick asked how will cars be towed in and out.
   Mr. Bakhoum stated the primary entrance will be off of 102nd
  street. He stated that the access will not be directly off of
  Hawthorne.

Chairman Springs open up the floor for comments from the public.

  2
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
September 2, 2020

The AT&T Operator opened the lines of communication to the public
in order for anyone on the line to speak for or against this project.

FOR / AGAINST:
None

Chairman Springs closed this segment and asked if there was a motion
on the floor.

MOTION:

Commissioner Patrick made the motion to affirm the categorical
exemption EA-CE-2019-091 and to adopt the attached resolution
approving SP-2020-008 subject to the 18 conditions. Commissioner
Trejo seconded the motion that Resolution No. 1882;

  A RESOULUTION OF THE CITY PLANNING COMMISSION OF THE
  CITY OF INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA, APPROVING A CERTAIN
  SPECIAL USE PERMIT FOR NAGY BAKHOUM, REPRESENTING B
  & H TOW, TO ALLOW TOWING SERVICE ON AN APPROXIMATELY
  34,353 SQUARE-FOOT, C-S (COMMERCIAL SERVICE) ZONED
  PROPERTY LOCATED AT 10201 HAWTHORNE BOULEVARD

Be approved.

The motion passed by the following roll call vote:

Ayes:  Commissioners Patrick, Rice, Trejo, Shaw-Williams and
  Chairman Springs

Ms. Wilcox explained the appeal process.

5B. SPECIAL USE PERMIT NO. 2020-009 (SP-2020-009) 401 SOUTH PRAIRIE
AVENUE: A public hearing to consider an application by Kevin Brown
for Special Use Permit No. 2020-009 (SP-2020-009) to allow exterior
alterations to an existing nonresidential structure in the Medical
Enterprise Overlay Zone that exceeds a valuation of twenty thousand
dollars ($20,000.00) on an approximately 1.27 acre, C-2 (General
Commercial) zoned property at 401 South Prairie Avenue.

Mr. Arturo Salazar, Planner made the staff presentation.

Chairman Springs asked the Planning Commission if there were any
questions for staff.

Commissioner Patrick asked if the building is fully occupied at this
time.
   Mr. Salazar stated that it was not at this time.

Commissioner Rice asked where the forty-two inch rail is going to
go.
   Mr. Salazar pointed out where the railing will be.

Commissioner Rice asked if the structure will remain an office
building.
   Mr. Salazar stated that currently the applicant does not have
  any tenants in mind and the applicant can answer that question.

Chairman Springs asked the applicant to tell everyone about the
project.

  3
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
September 2, 2020

The applicant stated that this project is a renovation of the exterior
of the building in an effort to bring it up to code for ADA purposes
as well as aesthetically to be more in line with the developments
that are coming along Prairie Ave. He stated the office building is
currently, mostly unoccupied and the owner wishes to get the exterior
ready for a potential future tenant.

Commissioner Trejo asked if the parking lot will be resurfaced.
   Mr. Salazar said the applicant is going to re-stripe the whole
  parking lot.

Commissioner Shaw-Williams asked if there will be a variety of
tenants or is it exclusively medical only.
   The applicant stated that there is no specific tenant that has
  been identified. He stated that it will mostly likely be related
  to the sports and entertainment industry.

Chairman Springs opened up the lines for individuals who are in favor
or against to speak.

The AT&T Operator opened the lines of communication to the public
in order for anyone on the line to speak for or against this project.

FOR / AGAINST:
None

Chairman Springs closed this segment and asked if there was a motion
on the floor.

MOTION:

Commissioner Rice made the motion to affirm the categorical exemption
EA-CE-2020-047 and to adopt the attached resolution approving
SP-2020-009 subject to the 11 conditions. Commissioner Patrick
seconded the motion that Resolution No. 1883;

  A RESOULUTION OF THE CITY PLANNING COMMISSION
  OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA, APPROVING
  A CERTAIN SPECIAL USE PERMIT FOR KEVIN BROWN TO
  ALLOW EXTERIOR ALTERATIONS TO AN EXISTING
  NONRESIDENTIAL STRUCTURE IN THE MEDICAL OVERLAY
  ZONE THAT EXCEEDS A VALUATION OF TWENTY THOUSAND
  DOLLARS ($20,000.00) ON AN APPROXIMATELY 46,978
  SQUARE-FOOT, C-2 (GENERAL COMMERCIAL)MEDICAL
  ENTERPRISE OVERLAY ZONED PROPERTY LOATED AT 401
  NORTH PRAIRIE AVENUE

Be approved.

The motion passed by the following roll call vote:

Ayes:  Commissioners Patrick, Rice, Trejo, Shaw-Williams and
  Chairman Springs

Ms. Wilcox explained the appeal process.

5C: SPECIAL USE PERMIT NO. 2020-011 (SP-2020-011) 129 N. MARKET
STREET: A public hearing to consider an application by Johnathan
DeVeaux, Owner, for a Special Use Permit No. 2021-011 (SP-2020-011)
to allow the sale of distilled spirits within an existing restaurant
on a 3,742 square-foot H-C (Historic Core) zone property at 129 North
Market Street.

  4
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
September 2, 2020

Mr. Bernard McCrumby, Planner made the staff presentation.

Chairman Springs asked the Planning Commission if there were any
questions for staff.

Commissioner Patrick asked if the owner will be on the AT&T line to
answer questions.
   Mr. McCrumby said yes.

Commissioner Rice asked if there will be a dance floor or
entertainment.
   Mr. McCrumby stated the way the current floor plan is laid out
  there is no room for a dance floor. He stated that there is an
  existing 30 square foot stage that was approved under the
  previous floor plan and the applicant has stated that if they
  have any live entertainment, it would be Jazz. He stated that
  there is no proposal for any dancing.

Chairman Springs asked the applicant to tell everyone about the
project.

The applicant, Johnathan DeVeaux stated they are a sit-down
restaurant and they would like to have jazz while patrons are eating.

Commissioner Patrick asked if the alcohol will be served during the
business hours of operations from Monday-Sunday, 8:00am – 2:00am.
   Mr. DeVeaux stated that they would like to be open for breakfast
  lunch and dinner and they would like to serve champagne during
  breakfast.

Commissioner Rice asked how many cameras will be on the exterior front
and rear of the building.
   Mr. DeVeaux stated there is one camera in the front and one in
  the back.

Commissioner Trejo asked how much of the area does the outside camera
cover.
   Mr. DeVeaux stated that it covers the alley in the back.

Commissioner Trejo asked if there was any activities happening in
the front or back the cameras would catch it.
   Mr. DeVeaux stated yes it would.

Chairman Springs asked Staff is there a time that you can begin to
serve alcohol.
   Ms. Wilcox stated that typically for restaurant use it is
  limited to the hours of operation.
   Mr. Bernard stated that the State mandates that at 1:00am
  alcohol can no longer be served.

Chairman Springs asked if the name of the restaurant, was ‘The Wood
Sports Bar’.
   Mr. Deveaux stated it is a restaurant not a sports bar.

Chairman Springs open up the floor for comments from the public.

The AT&T Operator opened the lines of communication to the public
in order for anyone on the line to speak for or against this project.

(6) NON-PUBLIC HEARINGS:
6A. DESIGN REVIEW NO. 2020-004 (DR-2020-004) 201 NORTH LA BREA
AVENUE. A non-public hearing to consider an application by Joe
Gambill, representing Wood Partners, for Design Review No. 2020-004
(DR-2020-004) to approve the design proposal for a new 6-story,
144-unit residential building on an approximately 38,750 square foot
lot, H-C (Historic Core) zoned property at 201 North La Brea Avenue.
Ms. Marissa Fewell, Assistant Planner made the staff presentation.

Chairman Springs Larry asked the Planning Commission if there were
any questions for staff.

Commissioner Rice asked if there was an opening coming from the
